BiblicalUsage: ʼêybâh means hostility. It appears in Genesis, Numbers, and Ezekiel, and each time it carries that same plain sense. The word keeps that same sense wherever it appears.
TheologicalSignificance: I take ʼêybâh to mean that rebellion is not freedom; it is slavery to ourselves. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
